sources.title: WCAG 2.2
sources.supports: Normative web accessibility success criteria and conformance framework.
sources.limits: A scoped check is not a complete conformance evaluation; does not prescribe a visual style.

sources.title: Learning about users and their needs
sources.supports: Research user goals and treat stakeholder-only opinions as assumptions.
sources.limits: Written for government services; does not establish this product's user needs.

sources.title: Services for government users
sources.supports: Expert internal work can require rapid switching and information together.
sources.limits: Domain example supports an exception; does not justify any dense screen.

sources.title: 10 Usability Heuristics for User Interface Design
sources.supports: General inspection principles including consistency, status, recovery, and user language.
sources.limits: Rules of thumb, not a validated score or product-specific defect proof.

sources.title: Cards: UI-Component Definition
sources.supports: Cards suit summaries/heterogeneous browsing; consistent lists can aid search and comparison.
sources.limits: 2016 guidance; neither bans cards nor proves all tables better.

sources.title: Progressive Disclosure
sources.supports: Defer uncommon detail; staged sequences can fail for interdependent steps.
sources.limits: 2006 guidance; the split needs task evidence, not a universal feature limit.

sources.title: Aesthetic and Minimalist Design
sources.supports: Retain necessary task information and reduce irrelevant competition.
sources.limits: Minimalism as a heuristic is not a requirement for sparse visual styling.

sources.title: Information Scent: How Users Decide Where to Go Next
sources.supports: Labels, context, and prior experience help people choose routes.
sources.limits: Does not supply the right vocabulary for an unknown audience.

sources.title: Writing for user interfaces
sources.supports: Use user language, purposeful labels, and understandable questions.
sources.limits: Specific government-service conventions are not universal interface rules.

sources.title: Error message
sources.supports: Associate validation with fields and preserve entered information.
sources.limits: Service/eligibility failures need different recovery communication.

sources.title: Button
sources.supports: Action hierarchy and caution around unexplained disabled buttons.
sources.limits: A design-system recommendation, not a prohibition for every product.

sources.title: Data table guidelines
sources.supports: Tables have deliberate density variants and need sufficient usable space.
sources.limits: Carbon row dimensions are system-specific tokens, not WCAG guarantees.

sources.title: Charts
sources.supports: Chart purpose, labels, units, sources, and justified interactivity.
sources.limits: Editorial conventions need adapting for analytical/exploratory tools.

sources.title: Dashboards
sources.supports: Dashboards suit recurring high-level monitoring with maintainable data.
sources.limits: An overview can be unsuitable for explanation or detailed insight.

sources.title: Data visualizations
sources.supports: Readable familiar charts, equivalent data access, and clear intent.
sources.limits: Guidance-only examples are not guaranteed production components.

sources.title: Data visualisation: charts
sources.supports: Bar baseline, line-axis exceptions, discontinuities, and dual-axis risks.
sources.limits: Expert analytical needs can differ; explain transformations and alternatives.

sources.title: Web Vitals
sources.supports: Field metrics for loading, responsiveness, stability, and p75 thresholds.
sources.limits: Metrics evolve and do not measure every task or backend wait.

sources.title: User-centric performance metrics
sources.supports: Performance varies by user/device; lab and field evidence differ.
sources.limits: A still image and load event cannot establish user performance.

sources.title: prefers-reduced-motion
sources.supports: Honor motion preferences through alternative animation treatments.
sources.limits: Reduced motion is broader than globally setting all durations to zero.

sources.title: ARIA Authoring Practices Guide
sources.supports: Accessible names, roles/states, keyboard patterns, and landmarks.
sources.limits: Informative guidance; examples need browser/assistive-technology validation.

sources.title: Understanding 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)
sources.supports: Text contrast thresholds, large-text definition, and exceptions.
sources.limits: Understanding is informative; apply the normative criterion in S01.

sources.title: Understanding 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast
sources.supports: Contrast for required component and graphical information.
sources.limits: Not every border, decorative shape, or chart color requires this ratio.

sources.title: Understanding 1.4.10 Reflow
sources.supports: Narrow-view reflow and scoped essential two-dimensional exceptions.
sources.limits: A table exception does not exempt surrounding headings or prose.

sources.title: Understanding 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)
sources.supports: 24 CSS px AA minimum plus spacing/equivalent/inline/UA/essential exceptions.
sources.limits: 44 CSS px is enhanced AAA, not the universal AA threshold.

sources.title: Understanding 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
sources.supports: AA prevents author content entirely hiding a focused component.
sources.limits: Full visibility is a stronger target; distinguish focus-indicator criteria.

sources.title: Understanding 2.1.1 Keyboard
sources.supports: Keyboard operation with exception for path-dependent functionality.
sources.limits: Exception concerns the function, not a preference for pointer input.

sources.title: Understanding 2.5.7 Dragging Movements
sources.supports: Single-pointer non-drag alternative unless essential or unmodified UA.
sources.limits: Keyboard access alone does not satisfy this pointer requirement.

sources.title: Understanding 3.1.2 Language of Parts
sources.supports: Programmatic language of passages/phrases with named exceptions.
sources.limits: Technical terms/proper names may be excepted; mixed language is not inherently failure.

sources.title: Understanding 4.1.3 Status Messages
sources.supports: Defined status updates should be programmatically available without taking focus.
sources.limits: Does not require every dynamic content change to be a live region.

sources.title: Understanding 1.4.1 Use of Color
sources.supports: Meaning should not depend on color alone.
sources.limits: Does not ban color as an additional visual cue.

sources.title: Understanding 1.4.4 Resize Text
sources.supports: 200% text resizing without content/function loss, with exceptions.
sources.limits: Do not treat a universal minimum font size as a WCAG rule.

sources.title: Understanding 2.4.13 Focus Appearance
sources.supports: Enhanced AAA focus indicator area and change-of-contrast requirements.
sources.limits: Separate this AAA criterion from AA focus visibility/obscuration checks.

sources.title: Guidelines for Human-AI Interaction, CHI 2019
sources.supports: Guideline development/evaluation for capability, fallibility, correction, and control in AI interaction.
sources.limits: Guideline validation does not prove this skill or detect AI-generated interfaces.

sources.title: Material 3: Applying typography
sources.supports: Indexed official excerpt supports platform/density/resizing-aware type decisions.
sources.limits: Full page extraction unavailable; do not attribute uninspected details or exact token values.

sources.title: Human Interface Guidelines: Foundations
sources.supports: Official index establishes relevant foundations/platform topics.
sources.limits: Only the index was readable; not substantive evidence for specific Apple layout rules.
